next_step: Finalize 6-month reserved commit and sign term sheet; schedule pricing review with finance
notes: Background: large North American fintech using LLMs for agent chat, embeddings for search and reranking in loan underwriting pipelines.
Initial ask: predictable throughput for peak trading hours (09:00-11:30 ET) + tight 90th percentile latency SLOs for chat (target 120ms p90 per token).

Sizing hypothesis: baseline steady-state traffic ~150 concurrent chat sessions, bursts to 700 requests/minute during peaks. Embeddings batch jobs nightly (500k vectors) with low latency constraints but high throughput needs.

Reserved capacity ask: evaluate 4x A100-80GB equiv GPUs vs 8x A100-40GB equiv; exploring mix for cost vs headroom. Preference to pin dedicated for critical routes and use hosted fallback for overflow.
Cost modeling summary (POC numbers): commit levels considered = 3, 6, 12 months. Finance wants per-month committed GPU SKU pricing and per-token unit economics under utilization assumptions.
Utilization assumptions used in model: 60% baseline utilization, 20% reserve buffer for autoscale, 20% idle for maintenance/rollouts. Also scenario sensitivity tested at 45% and 75% utilization.

Unit economics: modeled token-level costs across 3 scenarios (low/expected/high): expected unit cost estimated $0.00035 per prompt token and $0.00055 per completion token under 6-month commit at 65% utilization with batching and KV caching enabled.
Key levers in model: batching window (5-20ms), prefix cache hit rate (20-60%), quantized model variant mix (FP16 vs 4-bit), routing to lower-cost model for non-critical traffic.

SLA asks: 99.95% monthly uptime for dedicated pool, p95 latency guarantees per model route, credits table requested for missed SLOs. Legal flagged need for explicit outage definition and maintenance windows.
POC milestones: 1) perf baseline with 2 GPU nodes (Mar week 1), 2) full load test with synthetic peak traffic (Mar week 3), 3) cost runbook and handover to finance (Apr week 1).

Recent meetings: 2026-02-18 kickoff w/ platform + infra (notes in ff_2026-02-18_0932_sapphire_eval). 2026-03-02 deep dive on throughput targets and fallback routing (ff_2026-03-02_1415_capacity_call).
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable per-token costs for forecasting. If reserved capacity reduces unit cost by >25% vs hosted, finance will push for commit.'
Technical concerns raised by SE: 'KV cache hit rate in production unknown — model-level cache instrumentation required. If cache hit <30% economics change materially.'
Procurement path: prefer 6-month pilot then annual commit if utilization and SLOs met. Finance requires a three-scenario TCO (conservative/expected/optimistic) to greenlight commit >$200k ARR.
Open security items: produce SOC2 attestation copy, confirm KMS integration flow for key wrapping, provide demo of audit log retention UI (requested retention 7 years for some flows).

Negotiation points for AE to drive: 1) flexible commit ramp (quarterly add-ons), 2) SLA credit schedule tied to p95/p99 latencies, 3) right to burst to hosted at pre-agreed rate without data egress costs.

Action items assigned: Ethan -> finalize commercial term sheet draft (due 2026-03-12); Priya -> run sensitivity matrix on cache hit and batching; Diego -> prepare CSM handoff checklist and onboarding timeline.
Blocker notes: finance wants explicit modeling of burst costs when dedicated pool hits 95% utilization; legal redlines on SLA credit cap (they want no cap for critical services).
Decision criteria: finance will accept commit if 6-month pilot shows unit cost reduction >=20% with p90 latency <= 160ms and no severity-1 outages in pilot window.

Recommended Redwood posture: offer 6-month reserve with monthly observability deliverables, include automated cost reporting and token-level billing export, include canary fallback rules to hosted API to simplify procurement risk.
